# Viewport in ratatui - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/ratatui/0.30.2/ratatui/enum.Viewport.html

## Expand description

The area of the terminal that Ratatui draws into.

A [ Viewport](https://docs.rs/enum.Viewport.html) controls where widgets render and what

[returns.](https://docs.rs/struct.Frame.html#method.area)

`Frame::area`For a higher-level overview of viewports in the context of an application (including
examples), see [ Terminal](https://docs.rs/struct.Terminal.html).

Choose a viewport based on how the Ratatui UI should fit into the terminal:

- `Viewport::Fullscreen`
- `Viewport::Inline`
- `Viewport::Fixed`

In fullscreen mode, the viewport starts at (0, 0). In inline and fixed mode, the viewport may
have a non-zero `x`/`y` origin; prefer using `Frame::area()` as your root layout rectangle.
Code that assumes `(0, 0)` as the origin is therefore only correct for fullscreen viewports.

See [ Terminal::with_options](https://docs.rs/struct.Terminal.html#method.with_options) for how to select a viewport, and

[/](https://docs.rs/struct.Terminal.html#method.resize)

`Terminal::resize`[for resize behavior.](https://docs.rs/struct.Terminal.html#method.autoresize)

`Terminal::autoresize`[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use ratatui::backend::CrosstermBackend;
use ratatui::layout::{Constraint, Layout, Rect};
use ratatui::{Terminal, TerminalOptions, Viewport};
let mut terminal = Terminal::with_options(
    CrosstermBackend::new(std::io::stdout()),
    TerminalOptions {
        viewport: Viewport::Fixed(Rect::new(10, 5, 20, 4)),
    },
)?;
terminal.draw(|frame| {
    // `frame.area()` is `Rect::new(10, 5, 20, 4)`, not `(0, 0, 20, 4)`.
    let [title, body] =
        Layout::vertical([Constraint::Length(1), Constraint::Min(0)]).areas(frame.area());
    frame.render_widget("panel title", title);
    frame.render_widget("render the body relative to the fixed viewport", body);
})?;
```
## Variants[§](https://docs.rs#variants)

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Fullscreen)

### Fullscreen

Draw into the entire terminal.

This is the default viewport used by [ Terminal::new](https://docs.rs/struct.Terminal.html#method.new).

Choose this when the Ratatui app should own the whole terminal window.

When the terminal size changes, Ratatui automatically resizes internal buffers during
[ Terminal::draw](https://docs.rs/struct.Terminal.html#method.draw) /

[.](https://docs.rs/struct.Terminal.html#method.try_draw)

`Terminal::try_draw``Frame::area()` always starts at (0, 0).

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Inline)

### Inline([u16](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u16.html))

Draw the application inline with the rest of the terminal output.

Choose this when the UI should appear inside a larger command-line flow instead of taking over the entire terminal.

The viewport spans the full terminal width and its top-left corner is anchored to column 0 of the current cursor row when the terminal is created and whenever it is recomputed during resize. Ratatui reserves space for the requested height; if the cursor is near the bottom of the screen, this may scroll the terminal so the viewport remains fully visible.

The height is specified in rows and is clamped to the current terminal height.

Inline viewports always span the full terminal width.

For the full inline rendering model, including output inserted above the UI, see the
“Inline Viewport” section on [ Terminal](https://docs.rs/struct.Terminal.html) and

[.](https://docs.rs/struct.Terminal.html#method.insert_before)

`Terminal::insert_before`[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Fixed)

### Fixed([Rect](https://docs.rs/prelude/struct.Rect.html))

Draw into a fixed region of the terminal.

Choose this when Ratatui is responsible for only part of the screen, for example a panel in a larger terminal layout managed by another renderer or by surrounding application code.

Fixed viewports are not automatically resized. If the region should change (for example, on
terminal resize), call [ Terminal::resize](https://docs.rs/struct.Terminal.html#method.resize) yourself.

The area is specified as a [ Rect](https://docs.rs/prelude/struct.Rect.html) in terminal coordinates.

`Frame::area()` returns this rectangle as-is (including its `x`/`y` offset).
Ratatui does not keep this rectangle synchronized with backend resizes unless you call
[ Terminal::resize](https://docs.rs/struct.Terminal.html#method.resize) yourself.

See also [ Terminal::with_options](https://docs.rs/struct.Terminal.html#method.with_options) for initialization behavior.

# Terminal in ratatui - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/ratatui/0.30.2/ratatui/struct.Terminal.html

`pub struct Terminal<B>{ /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

An interface to interact and draw [ Frame](https://docs.rs/struct.Frame.html)s on the user’s terminal.

This is the main entry point for Ratatui’s rendering subsystem. It owns the backend-facing render state: double buffers, viewport bookkeeping, and cursor synchronization for each render pass.

If you’re building a fullscreen application with the `ratatui` crate’s default backend
([Crossterm](https://crates.io/crates/crossterm)), prefer [ ratatui::run](https://docs.rs/ratatui/latest/ratatui/fn.run.html) (or

[+](https://docs.rs/ratatui/latest/ratatui/fn.init.html)

`ratatui::init`[) over constructing](https://docs.rs/ratatui/latest/ratatui/fn.restore.html)

`ratatui::restore``Terminal` directly. These helpers enable common terminal modes (raw mode +
alternate screen) and restore them on exit and on panic.```
ratatui::run(|terminal| {
    let mut should_quit = false;
    while !should_quit {
        terminal.draw(|frame| {
            frame.render_widget("Hello, World!", frame.area());
        })?;
        // Handle events, update application state, and set `should_quit = true` to exit.
    }
    Ok(())
})?;
```
[§](https://docs.rs#typical-usage)Typical Usage

In a typical application, the flow is: set up a terminal, run an event loop, update state, and draw each frame.

- Choose a setup path for a `Terminal`. Most apps call`ratatui::run``Terminal`into your callback. If you need more control, use`ratatui::init``ratatui::restore``Terminal`manually via`Terminal::new``Terminal::with_options``Viewport`
- Enter your application’s event loop and call `Terminal::draw``Terminal::try_draw``Frame`
- Handle input and application state updates between draw calls.
- If the terminal is resized, call `Terminal::draw``draw`; fixed viewports require an explicit call to`Terminal::resize`

The normal mental model is: redraw the whole UI each pass, let Ratatui compute the diff, and
treat `Frame::area` as the source of truth for where this pass can render. Most application
code can stay entirely within that model.

[§](https://docs.rs#rendering-pipeline)Rendering Pipeline

A single call to [ Terminal::draw](https://docs.rs/struct.Terminal.html#method.draw) (or

[) represents one render pass. In broad strokes, Ratatui:](https://docs.rs/struct.Terminal.html#method.try_draw)

`Terminal::try_draw`- Checks whether the underlying terminal size changed (see `Terminal::autoresize`
- Creates a `Frame``Terminal::get_frame`
- Runs your render callback to populate that buffer.
- Diffs the current buffer against the previous buffer and writes the changes (see
`Terminal::flush`
- Applies cursor visibility and position requested by the frame (see
`Frame::set_cursor_position`
- Swaps the buffers to prepare for the next render pass (see `Terminal::swap_buffers`
- Flushes the backend (see `Backend::flush`

Each render pass starts with an empty buffer for the current viewport. Your render callback
should render everything that should be visible in [ Frame::area](https://docs.rs/struct.Frame.html#method.area), even if it is unchanged
from the previous frame. Ratatui diffs the current and previous buffers and only writes the
changes; anything you don’t render is treated as empty and may clear previously drawn content.

If the viewport size changes between render passes (for example via [ Terminal::autoresize](https://docs.rs/struct.Terminal.html#method.autoresize) or
an explicit

[), Ratatui clears the viewport and resets the previous buffer so the next](https://docs.rs/struct.Terminal.html#method.resize)

`Terminal::resize``draw` is treated as a full redraw.If [ Terminal::try_draw](https://docs.rs/struct.Terminal.html#method.try_draw) returns an error, the render pass ends early. Depending on where the
failure happened, Ratatui may have already resized internal buffers, written part of the diff,
or left cursor state unapplied. In most applications, treat that error as fatal for the current
terminal session and let higher-level setup code restore terminal state before continuing.

Most applications should use [ Terminal::draw](https://docs.rs/struct.Terminal.html#method.draw) /

[. Manual rendering is a separate, lower-level path intended primarily for tests and specialized integrations. In that mode you build a frame with](https://docs.rs/struct.Terminal.html#method.try_draw)

`Terminal::try_draw`[, apply the current buffer diff with](https://docs.rs/struct.Terminal.html#method.get_frame)

`Terminal::get_frame`[, then call](https://docs.rs/struct.Terminal.html#method.flush)

`Terminal::flush`[. If your backend buffers output, also call](https://docs.rs/struct.Terminal.html#method.swap_buffers)

`Terminal::swap_buffers`[.](https://docs.rs/backend/trait.Backend.html#tymethod.flush)

`Backend::flush`[ Terminal::flush](https://docs.rs/struct.Terminal.html#method.flush) only knows about Ratatui’s two screen buffers. It does not know whether
you have changed terminal modes or switched display surfaces (for example by leaving the
alternate screen). If you call it after such a change, Ratatui may replay a diff computed for
the old surface onto the new one. When you need a complete draw pass that stays synchronized
with cursor updates and backend flushing, prefer

[/](https://docs.rs/struct.Terminal.html#method.draw)

`Terminal::draw`[.](https://docs.rs/struct.Terminal.html#method.try_draw)

`Terminal::try_draw`The same caution applies to direct backend mutation and direct cursor manipulation. If you
write to the backend or move the cursor outside Ratatui’s normal render pass, the next draw may
overwrite those changes or may diff against stale assumptions. Use those escape hatches only
when you intentionally manage resynchronization yourself, typically by calling
[ Terminal::clear](https://docs.rs/struct.Terminal.html#method.clear) or performing a full render pass afterward.

```
use ratatui::Terminal;
use ratatui::backend::{Backend, TestBackend};
let backend = TestBackend::new(10, 10);
let mut terminal = Terminal::new(backend)?;
// Manual render pass (roughly what `Terminal::draw` does internally).
{
    let mut frame = terminal.get_frame();
    frame.render_widget("Hello World!", frame.area());
}
terminal.flush()?;
terminal.swap_buffers();
terminal.backend_mut().flush()?;
```
[§](https://docs.rs#viewports)Viewports

The viewport controls *where* Ratatui draws and therefore what [ Frame::area](https://docs.rs/struct.Frame.html#method.area) represents.
Most applications use

[, but Ratatui also supports](https://docs.rs/enum.Viewport.html#variant.Fullscreen)

`Viewport::Fullscreen`[and](https://docs.rs/enum.Viewport.html#variant.Inline)

`Viewport::Inline`[.](https://docs.rs/enum.Viewport.html#variant.Fixed)

`Viewport::Fixed`Choose a viewport based on how the app should fit into the terminal:

- `Viewport::Fullscreen`
- `Viewport::Inline`
- `Viewport::Fixed`

Choose a viewport at initialization time with [ Terminal::with_options](https://docs.rs/struct.Terminal.html#method.with_options) and

[.](https://docs.rs/struct.TerminalOptions.html)

`TerminalOptions``Frame::area` depends on the active viewport. In fullscreen mode it starts at (0, 0); in fixed
and inline mode it may have a non-zero origin, so prefer using `frame.area()` as your root
layout rectangle. The variant docs on [ Viewport](https://docs.rs/enum.Viewport.html) describe each mode in more detail, and
inline-specific behavior is covered in the “Inline Viewport” section below.

```
use ratatui::backend::CrosstermBackend;
use ratatui::layout::{Constraint, Layout, Rect};
use ratatui::{Terminal, TerminalOptions, Viewport};
// Fullscreen (most common):
let fullscreen = Terminal::new(CrosstermBackend::new(std::io::stdout()))?;
// Fixed region (your app manages the coordinates):
let viewport = Viewport::Fixed(Rect::new(0, 0, 30, 10));
let fixed = Terminal::with_options(
    CrosstermBackend::new(std::io::stdout()),
    TerminalOptions { viewport },
)?;
fixed.draw(|frame| {
    // Split the fixed viewport itself instead of assuming the viewport starts at `(0, 0)`.
    let [header, body] =
        Layout::vertical([Constraint::Length(1), Constraint::Min(0)]).areas(frame.area());
    frame.render_widget("Fixed panel header", header);
    frame.render_widget("Render the panel body relative to frame.area()", body);
})?;
```
Applications should redraw after terminal resizes with [ Terminal::draw](https://docs.rs/struct.Terminal.html#method.draw) /

[. Fullscreen and inline viewports resize automatically during those render passes; fixed viewports do not.](https://docs.rs/struct.Terminal.html#method.try_draw)

`Terminal::try_draw`If your event loop receives a resize event, treat that event as a signal to render again rather
than as a complete source of truth for layout. During a render pass, use [ Frame::area](https://docs.rs/struct.Frame.html#method.area) as the
rectangle that Ratatui has actually prepared for drawing. Ratatui checks the backend’s current
size during

`draw` / `try_draw` so layout reflects the terminal size that exists at render
time, even if resize events were coalesced, missed, or arrived before your app handled them.[§](https://docs.rs#inline-viewport)Inline Viewport

Inline mode is designed for applications that want to embed a UI into a larger CLI flow. In
[ Viewport::Inline](https://docs.rs/enum.Viewport.html#variant.Inline), Ratatui anchors the viewport to the backend cursor row and always starts
drawing at column 0.

To reserve vertical space for the requested height, Ratatui may append lines. When the cursor is near the bottom edge, terminals scroll; Ratatui accounts for that scrolling by shifting the computed viewport origin upward so the viewport stays fully visible.

While running in inline mode, [ Terminal::insert_before](https://docs.rs/struct.Terminal.html#method.insert_before) can be used to print output above the
viewport without disturbing the UI’s logical position. When Ratatui is built with the

`scrolling-regions` feature, `insert_before` can do this without clearing and redrawing the
viewport.```
use ratatui::{TerminalOptions, Viewport};
println!("Some output above the UI");
let options = TerminalOptions {
    viewport: Viewport::Inline(10),
};
let mut terminal = ratatui::try_init_with_options(options)?;
terminal.insert_before(1, |buf| {
    // Render a single line of output into `buf` before the UI.
    // (For example: logs, status updates, or command output.)
})?;
terminal.draw(|frame| {
    // Continue rendering the inline UI relative to the inline viewport.
    frame.render_widget("inline ui", frame.area());
})?;
```
[§](https://docs.rs#more-information)More Information

- Choosing a viewport: `Terminal::with_options``TerminalOptions``Viewport`
- The rendering pipeline: `Terminal::draw``Terminal::try_draw`
- Resize handling: `Terminal::autoresize``Terminal::resize`
- Cursor behavior: `Frame::set_cursor_position``Terminal::set_cursor_position``Terminal::show_cursor`
- Manual rendering and testing: `Terminal::get_frame``Terminal::flush``Terminal::swap_buffers`
- Printing above an inline UI: `Terminal::insert_before`

[§](https://docs.rs#initialization)Initialization

Most interactive TUIs need process-wide terminal setup (for example: raw mode and an alternate
screen) and matching teardown on exit and on panic. In Ratatui, that setup lives in the
`ratatui` crate; `Terminal` itself focuses on rendering and does not implicitly change those
modes.

If you’re using the `ratatui` crate with its default backend ([Crossterm](https://crates.io/crates/crossterm)), there are three
common entry points:

- `ratatui::run`- `ratatui::DefaultTerminal`
- `ratatui::init`- `ratatui::restore`- `run`, but you control the event loop and decide when to restore.
- `Terminal::new`- `Terminal::with_options`- [Termion](https://crates.io/crates/termion)/- [Termwiz](https://crates.io/crates/termwiz), inline UIs, or fixed viewports). You are responsible for terminal mode setup and teardown.

[ ratatui::run](https://docs.rs/ratatui/latest/ratatui/fn.run.html) was introduced in Ratatui 0.30, so older tutorials may use

`init`/`restore` or
manual construction.Some applications install a custom panic hook to log a crash report, print a friendlier error,
or integrate with error reporting. If you do, install it before calling [ ratatui::init](https://docs.rs/ratatui/latest/ratatui/fn.init.html) /

[. Ratatui wraps the current hook so it can restore terminal state first (for example: leaving the alternate screen and disabling raw mode) and then delegate to your hook.](https://docs.rs/ratatui/latest/ratatui/fn.run.html)

`ratatui::run`Crossterm is cross-platform and is what most Ratatui applications use by default. Ratatui also
supports other backends such as [Termion](https://crates.io/crates/termion) and [Termwiz](https://crates.io/crates/termwiz), and third-party backends can integrate
by implementing [ Backend](https://docs.rs/prelude/backend/index.html).

[§](https://docs.rs#how-it-works)How it works

`Terminal` ties together a [ Backend](https://docs.rs/prelude/backend/index.html), a

[, and a double-buffered diffing renderer. The high-level flow is described in the “Rendering Pipeline” section above; this section focuses on how that pipeline is implemented.](https://docs.rs/enum.Viewport.html)

`Viewport``Terminal` is generic over a [ Backend](https://docs.rs/prelude/backend/index.html) implementation and does not depend on a particular
terminal library. It relies on the backend to:

- report the current screen size (used by `Terminal::autoresize`
- draw cell updates (used by `Terminal::flush`
- clear regions (used by `Terminal::clear``Terminal::resize`
- move and show/hide the cursor (used by `Terminal::try_draw`
- optionally append lines (used by inline viewports and by `Terminal::insert_before`

[§](https://docs.rs#buffers-and-diffing)Buffers and diffing

The `Terminal` maintains two [ Buffer](https://docs.rs/prelude/struct.Buffer.html)s sized to the current viewport. During a render pass,
widgets draw into the “current” buffer via the

[passed to your callback. At the end of the pass,](https://docs.rs/struct.Frame.html)

`Frame`[diffs the current buffer against the previous buffer and sends only the changed cells to the backend.](https://docs.rs/struct.Terminal.html#method.flush)

`Terminal::flush`After flushing, [ Terminal::swap_buffers](https://docs.rs/struct.Terminal.html#method.swap_buffers) flips which buffer is considered “current” and resets
the next buffer. This is why each render pass starts from an empty buffer: your callback is
expected to fully redraw the viewport every time.

The [ CompletedFrame](https://docs.rs/struct.CompletedFrame.html) returned from

[/](https://docs.rs/struct.Terminal.html#method.draw)

`Terminal::draw`[provides a reference to the buffer that was just rendered, which can be useful for assertions in tests.](https://docs.rs/struct.Terminal.html#method.try_draw)

`Terminal::try_draw`[§](https://docs.rs#viewport-state-and-resizing)Viewport state and resizing

The active [ Viewport](https://docs.rs/enum.Viewport.html) controls how the viewport area is computed:

- Fullscreen: `Frame::area`covers the full backend size.
- Fixed: `Frame::area`is the exact rectangle you provided in terminal coordinates.
- Inline: `Frame::area`is a rectangle anchored to the backend cursor row.

For fullscreen and inline viewports, [ Terminal::autoresize](https://docs.rs/struct.Terminal.html#method.autoresize) checks the backend size during
every render pass and calls

[when it changes. Resizing updates the internal buffer sizes and clears the affected region; it also resets the previous buffer so the next draw is treated as a full redraw.](https://docs.rs/struct.Terminal.html#method.resize)

`Terminal::resize`[§](https://docs.rs#cursor-tracking)Cursor tracking

The cursor position requested by [ Frame::set_cursor_position](https://docs.rs/struct.Frame.html#method.set_cursor_position) is applied after

[so the cursor ends up on top of the rendered UI.](https://docs.rs/struct.Terminal.html#method.flush)

`Terminal::flush``Terminal` also tracks a
“last known cursor position” as a best-effort record of where it last wrote, and uses that
information when recomputing inline viewports on resize.[§](https://docs.rs#inline-specific-behavior)Inline-specific behavior

Inline viewports reserve vertical space by calling [ Backend::append_lines](https://docs.rs/backend/trait.Backend.html#method.append_lines). If the cursor is
close enough to the bottom edge, terminals scroll as lines are appended. Ratatui accounts for
that scrolling by shifting the computed viewport origin upward so the viewport remains fully
visible. On resize, Ratatui recomputes the inline origin while trying to keep the cursor at the
same relative row inside the viewport.

When Ratatui is built with the `scrolling-regions` feature, [ Terminal::insert_before](https://docs.rs/struct.Terminal.html#method.insert_before) uses
terminal scrolling regions to insert content above an inline viewport without clearing and
redrawing it.

## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

Returns a shared reference to the backend.

This is primarily useful for backend-specific inspection in tests (e.g. reading
[ TestBackend](https://docs.rs/backend/struct.TestBackend.html)’s buffer) or for backend-specific APIs that Ratatui does not model.

Reading from the backend does not desynchronize Ratatui, but values observed here may lag
behind the current render callback because Ratatui does not apply a frame to the backend
until the end of [ Terminal::draw](https://docs.rs/struct.Terminal.html#method.draw) /

[.](https://docs.rs/struct.Terminal.html#method.try_draw)

#### pub const fn [backend_mut](https://docs.rs#method.backend_mut)(&mut self) -> [&mut B](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.reference.html)

Returns a mutable reference to the backend.

This is an advanced escape hatch. Normal applications should render through
[ Terminal::draw](https://docs.rs/struct.Terminal.html#method.draw) /

[instead of mutating the backend directly.](https://docs.rs/struct.Terminal.html#method.try_draw)

`Terminal::try_draw`Use this when integrating with backend-specific APIs that Ratatui does not model, or when tests need direct control over backend state.

Mutating the backend directly can desynchronize Ratatui’s internal buffers, cursor
tracking, or viewport assumptions from what’s on-screen. If you do this, call
[ Terminal::clear](https://docs.rs/struct.Terminal.html#method.clear) or perform a full draw pass before relying on Ratatui’s view of the
terminal again.

Queries the real size of the backend.

This returns the backend’s current terminal size and does not update Ratatui’s internal
viewport bookkeeping by itself. The current renderable area depends on the configured
[ Viewport](https://docs.rs/enum.Viewport.html); use

[inside](https://docs.rs/struct.Frame.html#method.area)

`Frame::area`[/](https://docs.rs/struct.Terminal.html#method.draw)

`Terminal::draw`[if you want the area you should render into for the current pass.](https://docs.rs/struct.Terminal.html#method.try_draw)

`Terminal::try_draw`To make Ratatui observe backend size changes for fullscreen or inline viewports, see
[ Terminal::autoresize](https://docs.rs/struct.Terminal.html#method.autoresize).

Returns a [ Frame](https://docs.rs/struct.Frame.html) for manual rendering.

Most applications should render via [ Terminal::draw](https://docs.rs/struct.Terminal.html#method.draw) /

[. This is an escape hatch that exposes the frame construction step used by](https://docs.rs/struct.Terminal.html#method.try_draw)

`Terminal::try_draw`[so tests and advanced callers can render without running the full draw pipeline.](https://docs.rs/struct.Terminal.html#method.try_draw)

`Terminal::try_draw`This is primarily useful for tests, backend adapters, and specialized integrations that intentionally manage presentation themselves.

Unlike `draw` / `try_draw`, this does not call [ Terminal::autoresize](https://docs.rs/struct.Terminal.html#method.autoresize), does not write
updates to the backend, and does not apply any cursor changes. After rendering, you
typically call

[,](https://docs.rs/struct.Terminal.html#method.flush)

`Terminal::flush`[, and](https://docs.rs/struct.Terminal.html#method.swap_buffers)

`Terminal::swap_buffers`[.](https://docs.rs/backend/trait.Backend.html#tymethod.flush)

`Backend::flush`For the full render-pass behavior that also handles resizing, cursor updates, buffer
swapping, and backend flushing, see [ Terminal::draw](https://docs.rs/struct.Terminal.html#method.draw) and

[.](https://docs.rs/struct.Terminal.html#method.try_draw)

`Terminal::try_draw`The returned `Frame` mutably borrows the current buffer, so it must be dropped before you
can call methods like [ Terminal::flush](https://docs.rs/struct.Terminal.html#method.flush). The example below uses a scope to make that
explicit.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use ratatui::Terminal;
use ratatui::backend::{Backend, TestBackend};
let backend = TestBackend::new(30, 5);
let mut terminal = Terminal::new(backend)?;
{
    let mut frame = terminal.get_frame();
    frame.render_widget("Hello", frame.area());
}
// When not using `draw`, present the buffer manually:
terminal.flush()?;
terminal.swap_buffers();
terminal.backend_mut().flush()?;
```

Gets the current buffer as a mutable reference.

This is the buffer that the next [ Frame](https://docs.rs/struct.Frame.html) will render into (see

`Frame::buffer_mut`Mutating this buffer does not update the backend immediately. The changes become visible
only after a later [ Terminal::flush](https://docs.rs/struct.Terminal.html#method.flush) or full draw pass applies the diff. Because this
bypasses the usual render callback structure, it is mainly useful for tests and specialized
integrations that intentionally manage presentation themselves.

Applies the current buffer diff to the backend’s active display surface.

This compares the current buffer with the previous buffer and passes only the changed cells
to [ Backend::draw](https://docs.rs/backend/trait.Backend.html#tymethod.draw). It is one of the building blocks used by

[/](https://docs.rs/struct.Terminal.html#method.draw)

`Terminal::draw`[.](https://docs.rs/struct.Terminal.html#method.try_draw)

`Terminal::try_draw`This method does not swap buffers, does not update cursor visibility or position, and does
not call [ Backend::flush](https://docs.rs/backend/trait.Backend.html#tymethod.flush). See

[and](https://docs.rs/struct.Terminal.html#method.swap_buffers)

`Backend::flush``Terminal::flush` only reasons about Ratatui’s internal buffers. It does not know whether
the backend’s display surface changed since the last render pass. For example, if you leave
the alternate screen and then call `Terminal::flush`, Ratatui may replay a diff that was
computed for the alternate screen onto the main screen. In normal applications, prefer
[ Terminal::draw](https://docs.rs/struct.Terminal.html#method.draw) /

[unless you are intentionally managing the whole render pipeline yourself.](https://docs.rs/struct.Terminal.html#method.try_draw)

`Terminal::try_draw`Implementation note: when there are updates, Ratatui records the position of the last updated cell as the “last known cursor position”. Inline viewports use this to preserve the cursor’s relative position within the viewport across resizes.

`Terminal::flush`Clear the terminal and force a full redraw on the next draw call.

What gets cleared depends on the active [ Viewport](https://docs.rs/enum.Viewport.html):

- `Viewport::Fullscreen`
- `Viewport::Fixed`
- `Viewport::Inline`

Current behavior: for [ Viewport::Inline](https://docs.rs/enum.Viewport.html#variant.Inline), clearing runs from the viewport origin through
the end of the visible display area, not just the viewport’s rectangle. This is an
implementation detail rather than a contract; do not rely on it.

This preserves the backend’s current cursor position.

This also resets the “previous” buffer so the next [ Terminal::flush](https://docs.rs/struct.Terminal.html#method.flush) redraws the full
viewport.

```

    ratatui::restore();

`Backend`[.](https://docs.rs/struct.TerminalOptions.html)

`TerminalOptions`The viewport determines what area is exposed to widgets via [ Frame::area](https://docs.rs/struct.Frame.html#method.area) and how Ratatui
keeps its internal buffers synchronized with the backend. See

[for an overview of the available modes.](https://docs.rs/enum.Viewport.html)

`Viewport`For viewport behavior after initialization, see [ Terminal::resize](https://docs.rs/struct.Terminal.html#method.resize) and

`Terminal::try_draw`Resize behavior depends on the selected viewport:

- `Viewport::Fixed`- `Terminal::resize`

[§](https://docs.rs#example-2)Example

```
use std::io::stdout;
use ratatui::backend::CrosstermBackend;
use ratatui::layout::Rect;
use ratatui::{Terminal, TerminalOptions, Viewport};
let backend = CrosstermBackend::new(stdout());
let viewport = Viewport::Fixed(Rect::new(0, 0, 10, 10));
let _terminal = Terminal::with_options(backend, TerminalOptions { viewport })?;
```
When the viewport is [ Viewport::Inline](https://docs.rs/enum.Viewport.html#variant.Inline), Ratatui anchors the viewport to the current
cursor row at initialization time (always starting at column 0). Ratatui may append lines
and thereby scroll the terminal to make enough room for the requested height so the
viewport stays fully visible.

[Source](https://docs.rs/ratatui-core/0.1.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/ratatui_core/terminal/inline.rs.html#109-111)

[Source](https://docs.rs/ratatui-core/0.1.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/ratatui_core/terminal/inline.rs.html#109-111)

Insert some content before the current inline viewport. This has no effect when the viewport is not inline.

This is intended for inline UIs that want to print output (e.g. logs or status messages)
above the UI without breaking it. See [ Viewport::Inline](https://docs.rs/enum.Viewport.html#variant.Inline) for how inline viewports are
anchored.

The `draw_fn` closure will be called to draw into a writable `Buffer` that is `height`
lines tall. The content of that `Buffer` will then be inserted before the viewport.

When Ratatui is built with the `scrolling-regions` feature, this can be done without
clearing and redrawing the viewport. Without `scrolling-regions`, Ratatui falls back to a
more portable approach and clears the viewport so the next [ Terminal::draw](https://docs.rs/struct.Terminal.html#method.draw) /

[repaints it.](https://docs.rs/struct.Terminal.html#method.try_draw)

`Terminal::try_draw`If the viewport isn’t yet at the bottom of the screen, inserted lines will push it towards the bottom. Once the viewport is at the bottom of the screen, inserted lines will scroll the area of the screen above the viewport upwards.

Before:

```
+---------------------+
| pre-existing line 1 |
| pre-existing line 2 |
+---------------------+
|       viewport      |
+---------------------+
|                     |
|                     |
+---------------------+
```
After inserting 2 lines:

```
+---------------------+
| pre-existing line 1 |
| pre-existing line 2 |
|   inserted line 1   |
|   inserted line 2   |
+---------------------+
|       viewport      |
+---------------------+
+---------------------+
```
After inserting 2 more lines:

```
+---------------------+
| pre-existing line 2 |
|   inserted line 1   |
|   inserted line 2   |
|   inserted line 3   |
|   inserted line 4   |
+---------------------+
|       viewport      |
+---------------------+
```
If more lines are inserted than there is space on the screen, then the top lines will go directly into the terminal’s scrollback buffer. At the limit, if the viewport takes up the whole screen, all lines will be inserted directly into the scrollback buffer.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

[§](https://docs.rs#insert-a-single-line-before-the-current-viewport)Insert a single line before the current viewport

```
use ratatui::backend::{Backend, TestBackend};
use ratatui::layout::Position;
use ratatui::style::{Color, Style};
use ratatui::text::{Line, Span};
use ratatui::widgets::Widget;
use ratatui::{Terminal, TerminalOptions, Viewport};
let mut backend = TestBackend::new(10, 10);
// Simulate existing output above the inline UI.
backend.set_cursor_position(Position::new(0, 3))?;
let mut terminal = Terminal::with_options(
    backend,
    TerminalOptions {
        viewport: Viewport::Inline(4),
    },
)?;
terminal.insert_before(1, |buf| {
    Line::from(vec![
        Span::raw("This line will be added "),
        Span::styled("before", Style::default().fg(Color::Blue)),
        Span::raw(" the current viewport"),
    ])
    .render(buf.area, buf);
})?;
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/ratatui-core/0.1.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/ratatui_core/terminal/render.rs.html#81-83)#### pub fn [draw](https://docs.rs#method.draw)<F>(
    &mut self,
    render_callback: F,

[Source](https://docs.rs/ratatui-core/0.1.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/ratatui_core/terminal/render.rs.html#81-83)

#### pub fn [draw](https://docs.rs#method.draw)<F>(
    &mut self,
    render_callback: F,
) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[CompletedFrame](https://docs.rs/struct.CompletedFrame.html)<'_>, <B as [Backend](https://docs.rs/backend/trait.Backend.html)>::[Error](https://docs.rs/backend/trait.Backend.html#associatedtype.Error)>

Draws a single frame to the terminal.

Returns a [ CompletedFrame](https://docs.rs/struct.CompletedFrame.html) if successful, otherwise a backend error (

`B::Error`).If the render callback passed to this method can fail, use [ try_draw](https://docs.rs/struct.Terminal.html#method.try_draw) instead.

Applications should call `draw` or [ try_draw](https://docs.rs/struct.Terminal.html#method.try_draw) in a loop to continuously render the
terminal. These methods are the main entry points for drawing to the terminal.

The [ Frame](https://docs.rs/struct.Frame.html) passed to the render callback represents the currently configured

[(see](https://docs.rs/enum.Viewport.html)

`Viewport`[and](https://docs.rs/struct.Frame.html#method.area)

`Frame::area`[).](https://docs.rs/struct.Terminal.html#method.with_options)

`Terminal::with_options`Build layout relative to the [ Rect](https://docs.rs/prelude/struct.Rect.html) returned by

[rather than assuming the origin is](https://docs.rs/struct.Frame.html#method.area)

`Frame::area``(0, 0)`, so the same rendering code works for fixed and inline viewports.This method will:

- call `Terminal::autoresize`
- call the render callback, passing it a `Frame`
- call `Terminal::flush`
- show/hide the cursor based on `Frame::set_cursor_position`
- call `Terminal::swap_buffers`
- call `Backend::flush`
- return a `CompletedFrame`

If any backend step fails, the error is returned immediately and later steps in the render pass are skipped.

The [ CompletedFrame](https://docs.rs/struct.CompletedFrame.html) returned by this method can be useful for debugging or testing
purposes, but it is often not used in regular applications.

The render callback should fully render the entire frame when called, including areas that are unchanged from the previous frame. This is because each frame is compared to the previous frame to determine what has changed, and only the changes are written to the terminal. If the render callback does not fully render the frame, the terminal will not be in a consistent state.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-1)Examples

```
use ratatui::backend::TestBackend;
use ratatui::layout::Position;
use ratatui::{Frame, Terminal};
let backend = TestBackend::new(10, 10);
let mut terminal = Terminal::new(backend)?;
// With a closure.
terminal.draw(|frame| {
    let area = frame.area();
    frame.render_widget("Hello World!", area);
    frame.set_cursor_position(Position { x: 0, y: 0 });
})?;
// Or with a function.
terminal.draw(render)?;
fn render(frame: &mut Frame<'_>) {
    frame.render_widget("Hello World!", frame.area());
}
```

[Source](https://docs.rs/ratatui-core/0.1.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/ratatui_core/terminal/render.rs.html#189-192)

#### pub fn [try_draw](https://docs.rs#method.try_draw)<F, E>(
    &mut self,
    render_callback: F,
) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[CompletedFrame](https://docs.rs/struct.CompletedFrame.html)<'_>, <B as [Backend](https://docs.rs/backend/trait.Backend.html)>::[Error](https://docs.rs/backend/trait.Backend.html#associatedtype.Error)>

Tries to draw a single frame to the terminal.

Returns [ Result::Ok](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html#variant.Ok) containing a

[if successful, otherwise](https://docs.rs/struct.CompletedFrame.html)

`CompletedFrame`[containing the backend error (](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html#variant.Err)

`Result::Err``B::Error`) that caused the failure.This is the equivalent of [ Terminal::draw](https://docs.rs/struct.Terminal.html#method.draw) but the render callback is a function or
closure that returns a

`Result` instead of nothing.Applications should call `try_draw` or [ draw](https://docs.rs/struct.Terminal.html#method.draw) in a loop to continuously render the
terminal. These methods are the main entry points for drawing to the terminal.

The [ Frame](https://docs.rs/struct.Frame.html) passed to the render callback represents the currently configured

[(see](https://docs.rs/enum.Viewport.html)

`Viewport`[and](https://docs.rs/struct.Frame.html#method.area)

`Frame::area`[).](https://docs.rs/struct.Terminal.html#method.with_options)

`Terminal::with_options`Build layout relative to the [ Rect](https://docs.rs/prelude/struct.Rect.html) returned by

[rather than assuming the origin is](https://docs.rs/struct.Frame.html#method.area)

`Frame::area``(0, 0)`, so the same rendering code works for fixed and inline viewports.This method will:

- call `Terminal::autoresize`
- call the render callback, passing it a `Frame`
- call `Terminal::flush`
- show/hide the cursor based on `Frame::set_cursor_position`
- call `Terminal::swap_buffers`
- call `Backend::flush`
- return a `CompletedFrame`

If the render callback returns an error, Ratatui leaves the backend, buffers, cursor state, and frame count unchanged.

The render callback passed to `try_draw` can return any [ Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html) with an error type that
can be converted into

`B::Error` using the [trait. This makes it possible to use the](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/convert/trait.Into.html)

`Into``?` operator to propagate errors that occur during rendering. If the render callback returns
an error, the error will be returned from `try_draw` and the terminal will not be updated.The [ CompletedFrame](https://docs.rs/struct.CompletedFrame.html) returned by this method can be useful for debugging or testing
purposes, but it is often not used in regular applications.

The render callback should fully render the entire frame when called, including areas that are unchanged from the previous frame. This is because each frame is compared to the previous frame to determine what has changed, and only the changes are written to the terminal. If the render function does not fully render the frame, the terminal will not be in a consistent state.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-2)Examples

```
use std::io;
use ratatui::backend::CrosstermBackend;
use ratatui::layout::Position;
use ratatui::{Frame, Terminal};
let backend = CrosstermBackend::new(std::io::stdout());
let mut terminal = Terminal::new(backend)?;
// With a closure that returns `Result`.
terminal.try_draw(|frame| -> io::Result<()> {
    let _value: u8 = "42".parse().map_err(io::Error::other)?;
    let area = frame.area();
    frame.render_widget("Hello World!", area);
    frame.set_cursor_position(Position { x: 0, y: 0 });
    Ok(())
})?;
// Or with a function.
terminal.try_draw(render)?;
fn render(frame: &mut Frame<'_>) -> io::Result<()> {
    frame.render_widget("Hello World!", frame.area());
    Ok(())
}
```

Updates the Terminal so that internal buffers match the requested area.

This updates the buffer size used for rendering and triggers a full clear so the next
[ Terminal::draw](https://docs.rs/struct.Terminal.html#method.draw) /

[paints into a consistent area.](https://docs.rs/struct.Terminal.html#method.try_draw)

`Terminal::try_draw`When the viewport is [ Viewport::Inline](https://docs.rs/enum.Viewport.html#variant.Inline), the

`area` argument is treated as the new
terminal size and the viewport origin is recomputed relative to the current cursor position.
Ratatui attempts to keep the cursor at the same relative row within the viewport across
resizes.See also: [ Terminal::autoresize](https://docs.rs/struct.Terminal.html#method.autoresize) (automatic resizing during

[/](https://docs.rs/struct.Terminal.html#method.draw)

`Terminal::draw`[).](https://docs.rs/struct.Terminal.html#method.try_draw)

`Terminal::try_draw`For [ Viewport::Fixed](https://docs.rs/enum.Viewport.html#variant.Fixed) and

[,](https://docs.rs/enum.Viewport.html#variant.Fullscreen)

`Viewport::Fullscreen``area` becomes the new viewport area.
For [,](https://docs.rs/enum.Viewport.html#variant.Inline)

`Viewport::Inline``area` is interpreted as the backend’s new terminal size and the
viewport origin may move to preserve the cursor’s relative row within the inline UI.Queries the backend for size and resizes if it doesn’t match the previous size.

This is called automatically during [ Terminal::draw](https://docs.rs/struct.Terminal.html#method.draw) /

[for fullscreen and inline viewports. Fixed viewports are not automatically resized.](https://docs.rs/struct.Terminal.html#method.try_draw)

`Terminal::try_draw`If the size changed, this calls [ Terminal::resize](https://docs.rs/struct.Terminal.html#method.resize) and therefore clears the affected
region before the next frame is rendered.

# ratatui::init - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/ratatui/0.30.2/ratatui/init/index.html

**crate feature**only.

`crossterm`## Expand description

Terminal initialization and restoration functions.

This module provides a set of convenience functions for initializing and restoring terminal state when creating Ratatui applications. These functions handle the common setup and teardown tasks required for terminal user interfaces.

All functions in this module use the [ CrosstermBackend](https://docs.rs/backend/struct.CrosstermBackend.html) by default, which provides excellent
cross-platform compatibility and is the recommended backend for most applications. The

[type alias encapsulates this choice, providing a ready-to-use terminal configuration that works well across different operating systems. For more information about backend choices and alternatives, see the](https://docs.rs/type.DefaultTerminal.html)

`DefaultTerminal`[module.](https://docs.rs/backend/index.html)

`backend`Once you have initialized a terminal using the functions in this module, you can use it to
[draw the UI](https://docs.rs/index.html#drawing-the-ui) and [handle events](https://docs.rs/index.html#handling-events). For more
information about building widgets for your application, see the [ widgets](https://docs.rs/widgets/index.html)
module.

**Note**: All functions and types in this module are re-exported at the crate root for
convenience, so you can call `ratatui::run()`, `ratatui::init()`, etc. instead of
`ratatui::init::run()`, `ratatui::init::init()`, etc.

[§](https://docs.rs#which-function-should-i-start-with)Which function should I start with?

Start with the simplest path that fits your application:

- Use `run`
- Move to `init``restore`
- Use `try_init``try_restore`
- Use `init_with_options``try_init_with_options``TerminalOptions`
- Construct `Terminal`

[§](https://docs.rs#available-types-and-functions)Available Types and Functions

[§](https://docs.rs#types)Types

- `DefaultTerminal`- `Terminal<CrosstermBackend<Stdout>>`, providing a reasonable default terminal configuration for most applications. All initialization functions return this type.

[§](https://docs.rs#functions)Functions

The module provides several related functions that handle different initialization scenarios:

- `run`
- `init`
- `try_init`- `init`- `Result`instead of panicking.
- `init_with_options`- `TerminalOptions`
- `try_init_with_options`- `init_with_options`- `Result`instead of panicking.
- `restore`
- `try_restore`- `restore`- `Result`instead of printing errors.

[§](https://docs.rs#usage-guide)Usage Guide

Start with the normal fullscreen application path:

```
fn main() -> std::io::Result<()> {
    ratatui::run(|terminal| {
        loop {
            terminal.draw(|frame| frame.render_widget("Hello, world!", frame.area()))?;
            if crossterm::event::read()?.is_key_press() {
                break Ok(());
            }
        }
    })
}
```
Then add resize-aware redraws to the event loop:

```
use crossterm::event::{self, Event, KeyCode, KeyEventKind};
fn main() -> std::io::Result<()> {
    ratatui::run(|terminal| {
        loop {
            terminal.draw(|frame| {
                frame.render_widget("Resize the terminal or press q to quit", frame.area());
            })?;
            match event::read()? {
                Event::Resize(_, _) => {
                    // The next `draw` pass re-renders the UI at the new size.
                }
                Event::Key(key)
                    if key.kind == KeyEventKind::Press && key.code == KeyCode::Char('q') =>
                {
                    break Ok(());
                }
                _ => {}
            }
        }
    })
}
```
Reach for [ init](https://docs.rs/fn.init.html) /

[when you want manual control over setup and teardown:](https://docs.rs/fn.restore.html)

`restore````
// Using init() - panics on failure
let mut terminal = ratatui::init();
// ... app logic ...
ratatui::restore();
// Using try_init() - returns Result for custom error handling
let mut terminal = ratatui::try_init()?;
// ... app logic ...
ratatui::try_restore()?;
```
Use [ init_with_options](https://docs.rs/fn.init_with_options.html) when the UI should not use the normal fullscreen path, for example
for an inline UI that continues to share the terminal with earlier output:

```
use crossterm::event::{self, Event, KeyCode, KeyEventKind};
use ratatui::widgets::Widget;
use ratatui::{TerminalOptions, Viewport};
let options = TerminalOptions {
    viewport: Viewport::Inline(10),
};
let mut terminal = ratatui::init_with_options(options);
terminal.insert_before(1, |buf| {
    "> Ready".render(buf.area, buf);
})?;
loop {
    terminal.draw(|frame| {
        frame.render_widget("Inline UI lives below earlier terminal output", frame.area());
    })?;
    if matches!(
        event::read()?,
        Event::Key(key)
            if key.kind == KeyEventKind::Press && key.code == KeyCode::Char('q')
    ) {
        break;
    }
}
ratatui::restore();
// Using try_init_with_options() - returns Result for custom error handling
let options = TerminalOptions {
    viewport: Viewport::Inline(10),
};
let mut terminal = ratatui::try_init_with_options(options)?;
terminal.draw(|frame| {
    frame.render_widget("Inline UI", frame.area());
})?;
ratatui::try_restore()?;
```
These higher-level helpers are the normal application path. Manual [ Terminal](https://docs.rs/struct.Terminal.html) construction is
still available for custom backends and specialized integrations, but it is an advanced path.

For cleanup, use [ restore](https://docs.rs/fn.restore.html) in most cases where you want to attempt restoration but don’t need
to handle errors (they are printed to stderr). Use

[when you need to handle restoration errors, perhaps to retry or provide user feedback.](https://docs.rs/fn.try_restore.html)

`try_restore`Once you have a terminal set up, continue with the main loop to [draw the
UI](https://docs.rs/index.html#drawing-the-ui) and [handle events](https://docs.rs/index.html#handling-events). See the [main crate
documentation](https://docs.rs/index.html) for comprehensive examples of complete applications.

[§](https://docs.rs#key-differences)Key Differences

| Function | Alternate Screen | Raw Mode | Error Handling | Use Case |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `run` | ✓ | ✓ | Auto-cleanup | Simple apps |
| `init` | ✓ | ✓ | Panic | Standard full-screen apps |
| `try_init` | ✓ | ✓ | Result | Standard apps with error handling |
| `init_with_options` | ✗ | ✓ | Panic | Custom viewport apps |
| `try_init_with_options` | ✗ | ✓ | Result | Custom viewport with error handling |

[§](https://docs.rs#panic-hook)Panic Hook

All initialization functions install a panic hook that automatically restores the terminal state before panicking. This ensures that even if your application panics, the terminal will be left in a usable state.

**Important**: Call the initialization functions *after* installing any other panic hooks to
ensure the terminal is restored before other hooks run.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions-1)

- [init](https://docs.rs/fn.init.html)
- Initialize a terminal with reasonable defaults for most applications.
- [init_](https://docs.rs/fn.init_with_options.html)- with_ - options
- Initialize a terminal with the given options and reasonable defaults.
- [restore](https://docs.rs/fn.restore.html)
- Restores the terminal to its original state.
- [run](https://docs.rs/fn.run.html)
- Run a closure with a terminal initialized with reasonable defaults for most applications.
- [try_](https://docs.rs/fn.try_init.html)- init
- Try to initialize a terminal using reasonable defaults for most applications.
- [try_](https://docs.rs/fn.try_init_with_options.html)- init_ - with_ - options
- Try to initialize a terminal with the given options and reasonable defaults.
- [try_](https://docs.rs/fn.try_restore.html)- restore
- Restore the terminal to its original state.

## Type Aliases[§](https://docs.rs#types-1)

- [Default](https://docs.rs/type.DefaultTerminal.html)- Terminal
- A type alias for the default terminal type.

}## Expand description

The `Backend` trait provides an abstraction over different terminal libraries. It defines the
methods required to draw content, manipulate the cursor, and clear the terminal screen.

Most applications should not need to interact with the `Backend` trait directly as the
[ Terminal](https://docs.rs/ratatui/latest/ratatui/struct.Terminal.html) struct provides a higher level interface for interacting with the terminal.

## Required Associated Types[§](https://docs.rs#required-associated-types)

## Required Methods[§](https://docs.rs#required-methods)

Draw the given content to the terminal screen.

The content is provided as an iterator over `(u16, u16, &Cell)` tuples, where the first two
elements represent the x and y coordinates, and the third element is a reference to the
[ Cell](https://docs.rs/buffer/struct.Cell.html) to be drawn.

Get the current cursor position on the terminal screen.

The returned tuple contains the x and y coordinates of the cursor. The origin (0, 0) is at the top left corner of the screen.

See [ set_cursor_position](https://docs.rs/trait.Backend.html#tymethod.set_cursor_position) for an example.

Clears all character cells in the terminal’s visible display area.

This operation preserves the cursor position. If the cursor lies within the cleared region, the character cell at the cursor position is cleared. No guarantees are made about scrollback, history, or off-screen buffers.

This is equivalent to calling [ clear_region](https://docs.rs/trait.Backend.html#tymethod.clear_region) with

[.](https://docs.rs/enum.ClearType.html#variant.All)

`ClearType::All`[§](https://docs.rs#example-2)Example

Clears a specific region of the terminal’s visible display area, as defined by
[ ClearType](https://docs.rs/enum.ClearType.html).

This operation preserves the cursor position. If the cursor lies within the cleared region, the character cell at the cursor position is cleared. Clearing applies to the active display surface only and does not make guarantees about scrollback, history, or off-screen buffers.

This method is optional and may not be implemented by all backends. The default
implementation calls [ clear](https://docs.rs/trait.Backend.html#tymethod.clear) if the

`clear_type` is [and returns an error otherwise.](https://docs.rs/enum.ClearType.html#variant.All)

`ClearType::All`[§](https://docs.rs#example-3)Example

[§](https://docs.rs#errors)Errors

This method will return an error if the terminal screen could not be cleared. It will also
return an error if the `clear_type` is not supported by the backend.

#### fn [window_size](https://docs.rs#tymethod.window_size)(&mut self) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[WindowSize](https://docs.rs/struct.WindowSize.html), Self::[Error](https://docs.rs/trait.Backend.html#associatedtype.Error)>

Get the size of the terminal screen in columns/rows and pixels as a [ WindowSize](https://docs.rs/struct.WindowSize.html).

The reason for this not returning only the pixel size, given the redundancy with the
`size()` method, is that the underlying backends most likely get both values with one
syscall, and the user is also most likely to need columns and rows along with pixel size.

[Source](https://docs.rs/ratatui-core/0.1.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/ratatui_core/backend.rs.html#363-367)**crate feature **`scrolling-regions` only.

[Source](https://docs.rs/ratatui-core/0.1.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/ratatui_core/backend.rs.html#363-367)

**crate feature**only.

`scrolling-regions`Scroll a region of the screen upwards, where a region is specified by a (half-open) range of rows.

Each row in the region is replaced by the row `line_count` rows below it, except the bottom
`line_count` rows, which are replaced by empty rows. If `line_count` is equal to or larger
than the number of rows in the region, then all rows are replaced with empty rows.

If the region includes row 0, then `line_count` rows are copied into the bottom of the
scrollback buffer. These rows are first taken from the old contents of the region, starting
from the top. If there aren’t sufficient rows in the region, then the remainder are empty
rows.

The position of the cursor afterwards is undefined.

The behavior is designed to match what ANSI terminals do when scrolling regions are established. With ANSI terminals, a scrolling region can be established with the “^[[X;Yr” sequence, where X and Y define the lines of the region. The scrolling region can be reset to be the whole screen with the “^[[r” sequence.

When a scrolling region is established in an ANSI terminal, various operations’ behaviors are changed in such a way that the scrolling region acts like a “virtual screen”. In particular, the scrolling sequence “^[[NS”, which scrolls lines up by a count of N.

On an ANSI terminal, this method will probably translate to something like: “^[[X;Yr^[[NS^[[r”. That is, set the scrolling region, scroll up, then reset the scrolling region.

For examples of how this function is expected to work, refer to the tests for
[ TestBackend::scroll_region_up](https://docs.rs/struct.TestBackend.html#method.scroll_region_up).

[Source](https://docs.rs/ratatui-core/0.1.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/ratatui_core/backend.rs.html#388-392)**crate feature **`scrolling-regions` only.

[Source](https://docs.rs/ratatui-core/0.1.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/ratatui_core/backend.rs.html#388-392)

**crate feature**only.

`scrolling-regions`Scroll a region of the screen downwards, where a region is specified by a (half-open) range of rows.

Each row in the region is replaced by the row `line_count` rows above it, except the top
`line_count` rows, which are replaced by empty rows. If `line_count` is equal to or larger
than the number of rows in the region, then all rows are replaced with empty rows.

The position of the cursor afterwards is undefined.

See the documentation for [ Self::scroll_region_down](https://docs.rs/trait.Backend.html#tymethod.scroll_region_down) for more information about how this
is expected to be implemented for ANSI terminals. All of that applies, except the ANSI
sequence to scroll down is “^[[NT”.

This function is asymmetrical with regards to the scrollback buffer. The reason is that this how terminals seem to implement things.

For examples of how this function is expected to work, refer to the tests for
[ TestBackend::scroll_region_down](https://docs.rs/struct.TestBackend.html#method.scroll_region_down).

## Provided Methods[§](https://docs.rs#provided-methods)

Insert `n` line breaks to the terminal screen.

This method is optional and may not be implemented by all backends.

# Frame in ratatui - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/ratatui/0.30.2/ratatui/struct.Frame.html

`pub struct Frame<'a> { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

A consistent view into the terminal state for rendering a single frame.

You usually get a `Frame` from the closure argument of [ Terminal::draw](https://docs.rs/struct.Terminal.html#method.draw) /

[. For manual rendering, use](https://docs.rs/struct.Terminal.html#method.try_draw)

`Terminal::try_draw`[.](https://docs.rs/struct.Terminal.html#method.get_frame)

`Terminal::get_frame`A `Frame` is used to render widgets into Ratatui’s current buffer and request the cursor state
for the end of the render pass.

The changes drawn to the frame are applied only to the current [ Buffer](https://docs.rs/prelude/struct.Buffer.html). After the closure
returns, the current buffer is compared to the previous buffer and only the changed cells are
sent to the backend. This avoids drawing redundant cells.

## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

Returns the area of the current frame.

This is guaranteed not to change during rendering, so may be called multiple times.

If your app listens for a resize event from the backend, ignore that event’s dimensions for calculations performed during the current render callback and use this value instead. It is the area of the buffer that is actually being rendered for this pass.

[.](https://docs.rs/prelude/trait.Widget.html#tymethod.render)

`Widget::render`Usually the area argument is the size of the current frame or a sub-area of the current
frame (which can be obtained using [ Layout](https://docs.rs/prelude/struct.Layout.html) to split the total area).

Render a [ StatefulWidget](https://docs.rs/prelude/trait.StatefulWidget.html) to the current buffer using

[.](https://docs.rs/prelude/trait.StatefulWidget.html#tymethod.render)

`StatefulWidget::render`Usually the area argument is the size of the current frame or a sub-area of the current
frame (which can be obtained using [ Layout](https://docs.rs/prelude/struct.Layout.html) to split the total area).

The last argument should be an instance of the [ StatefulWidget::State](https://docs.rs/prelude/trait.StatefulWidget.html#associatedtype.State) associated to the
given

[.](https://docs.rs/prelude/trait.StatefulWidget.html)

`StatefulWidget`Like [ Frame::render_widget](https://docs.rs/struct.Frame.html#method.render_widget), this writes directly into the current frame buffer. The
widget owns how it interprets and mutates the provided state.

[§](https://docs.rs#example-1)Example

```
use ratatui_core::widgets::StatefulWidget;
struct DemoWidget;
impl StatefulWidget for DemoWidget {
    type State = bool;
    fn render(self, area: Rect, buf: &mut Buffer, state: &mut Self::State) {
        let symbol = if *state { "Y" } else { "N" };
        buf[(area.x, area.y)].set_symbol(symbol);
    }
}
let mut state = true;
let area = Rect::new(0, 0, 5, 5);
frame.render_stateful_widget(DemoWidget, area, &mut state);
```

coordinates. If this method is not called, the cursor will be hidden.

Note that this will interfere with calls to [ Terminal::hide_cursor](https://docs.rs/struct.Terminal.html#method.hide_cursor),

[, and](https://docs.rs/struct.Terminal.html#method.show_cursor)

`Terminal::show_cursor`[. Pick one of the APIs and stick with it.](https://docs.rs/struct.Terminal.html#method.set_cursor_position)

#### pub const fn [buffer_mut](https://docs.rs#method.buffer_mut)(&mut self) -> &mut [Buffer](https://docs.rs/prelude/struct.Buffer.html)

Gets the buffer that this `Frame` draws into as a mutable reference.

This is an escape hatch for direct buffer manipulation. Normal applications should prefer the widget rendering methods so layout and rendering intent stay visible at the call site.

Use this when tests, custom widgets, or specialized integrations need direct cell access during a render pass.

Changes written here are not visible on the backend until the render pass is applied by
[ Terminal::flush](https://docs.rs/struct.Terminal.html#method.flush) or a full

[/](https://docs.rs/struct.Terminal.html#method.draw)

`Terminal::draw`[pass.](https://docs.rs/struct.Terminal.html#method.try_draw)

`Terminal::try_draw`[§](https://docs.rs#example-2)Example

`frame.buffer_mut()[(0, 0)].set_symbol("h");`Returns the current frame count.

This method provides access to the frame count, which is a sequence number indicating how many frames have been rendered up to (but not including) this one. It can be used for purposes such as animation, performance tracking, or debugging.

Each time a frame has been rendered, this count is incremented,
providing a consistent way to reference the order and number of frames processed by the
terminal. When count reaches its maximum value (`usize::MAX`), it wraps around to zero.

This count is particularly useful when dealing with dynamic content or animations where the state of the display changes over time. By tracking the frame count, developers can synchronize updates or changes to the content with the rendering process.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
let current_count = frame.count();
println!("Current frame count: {}", current_count);
```

# Widget in ratatui::prelude - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/ratatui/0.30.2/ratatui/prelude/trait.Widget.html

```
pub trait Widget {
    // Required method
    fn
```
[render](https://docs.rs#tymethod.render)(self, area: [Rect](https://docs.rs/struct.Rect.html), buf: &mut [Buffer](https://docs.rs/struct.Buffer.html))
       where Self: [Sized](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/marker/trait.Sized.html);
}## Expand description

A `Widget` is a type that can be drawn on a [ Buffer](https://docs.rs/struct.Buffer.html) in a given

[.](https://docs.rs/struct.Rect.html)

`Rect`For a comprehensive guide to widgets, including trait explanations, implementation patterns,
and available widgets, see the [ widgets](https://docs.rs/ratatui/widgets/index.html) module documentation.

Prior to Ratatui 0.26.0, widgets generally were created for each frame as they were consumed
during rendering. This meant that they were not meant to be stored but used as *commands* to
draw common figures in the UI.

Starting with Ratatui 0.26.0, all the internal widgets implement Widget for a reference to themselves. This allows you to store a reference to a widget and render it later. Widget crates should consider also doing this to allow for more flexibility in how widgets are used.

In Ratatui 0.26.0, we also added an unstable `WidgetRef` trait and implemented this on all the
internal widgets. In addition to the above benefit of rendering references to widgets, this also
allows you to render boxed widgets. This is useful when you want to store a collection of
widgets with different types. You can then iterate over the collection and render each widget.
See [https://github.com/ratatui/ratatui/issues/1287](https://github.com/ratatui/ratatui/issues/1287) for more information.

In general where you expect a widget to immutably work on its data, we recommended to implement
`Widget` for a reference to the widget (`impl Widget for &MyWidget`). If you need to store state
between draw calls, implement `StatefulWidget` if you want the Widget to be immutable, or
implement `Widget` for a mutable reference to the widget (`impl Widget for &mut MyWidget`) if
you want the widget to be mutable. The mutable widget pattern is used infrequently in apps, but
can be quite useful.

A blanket implementation of `Widget` for `&W` where `W` implements `WidgetRef` is provided.
Widget is also implemented for `&str` and `String` types.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
use ratatui::{
    backend::TestBackend,
    widgets::{Clear, Widget},
    Terminal,
};
terminal.draw(|frame| {
    frame.render_widget(Clear, frame.area());
});
```
It’s common to render widgets inside other widgets:

```
use ratatui_core::buffer::Buffer;
use ratatui_core::layout::Rect;
use ratatui_core::text::Line;
use ratatui_core::widgets::Widget;
struct MyWidget;
impl Widget for MyWidget {
    fn render(self, area: Rect, buf: &mut Buffer) {
        Line::raw("Hello").render(area, buf);
    }
}
```

onto a [ Buffer](https://docs.rs/struct.Buffer.html) in a specified

[. The slice represents a static string which can be rendered by reference, thereby avoiding the need for string cloning or ownership transfer when drawing the text to the screen.](https://docs.rs/struct.Rect.html)

# Layout in ratatui::prelude - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/ratatui/0.30.2/ratatui/prelude/struct.Layout.html

`pub struct Layout { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

The primary layout engine for dividing terminal space using constraints and direction.

A layout is a set of constraints that can be applied to a given area to split it into smaller rectangular areas. This is the core building block for creating structured user interfaces in terminal applications.

A layout is composed of:

- a direction (horizontal or vertical)
- a set of constraints (length, ratio, percentage, fill, min, max)
- a margin (horizontal and vertical), the space between the edge of the main area and the split areas
- a flex option that controls space distribution
- a spacing option that controls gaps between segments

The algorithm used to compute the layout is based on the [ kasuari](https://crates.io/crates/kasuari) solver, a linear constraint
solver that computes positions and sizes to satisfy as many constraints as possible in order of
their priorities.

When the layout is computed, the result is cached in a thread-local cache, so that subsequent
calls with the same parameters are faster. The cache is a `LruCache`, and the size of the cache
can be configured using [ Layout::init_cache()](https://docs.rs/struct.Layout.html#method.init_cache) when the

`layout-cache` feature is enabled.[§](https://docs.rs#construction)Construction

- `default`
- `new`
- `vertical`
- `horizontal`

[§](https://docs.rs#configuration)Configuration

- `direction`
- `constraints`
- `margin`
- `horizontal_margin`
- `vertical_margin`
- `flex`
- `spacing`

[§](https://docs.rs#layout-operations)Layout Operations

- `areas`
- `spacers`
- `split`
- `split_with_spacers`

[§](https://docs.rs#cache-management)Cache Management

- `init_cache`

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use ratatui_core::buffer::Buffer;
use ratatui_core::layout::{Constraint, Direction, Layout, Rect};
use ratatui_core::text::Text;
use ratatui_core::widgets::Widget;
fn render(area: Rect, buf: &mut Buffer) {
    let layout = Layout::vertical([Constraint::Length(5), Constraint::Fill(1)]);
    let [top, bottom] = layout.areas(area);
    Text::from("foo").render(top, buf);
    Text::from("bar").render(bottom, buf);
}
```
See the `layout`, `flex`, and `constraints` examples in the [Examples](https://github.com/ratatui/ratatui/blob/main/examples/README.md) folder for more details
about how to use layouts.

For comprehensive layout documentation and examples, see the [ layout](https://docs.rs/layout/index.html) module.

## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

[Source](https://docs.rs/ratatui-core/0.1.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/ratatui_core/layout/layout.rs.html#218)#### pub const [DEFAULT_CACHE_SIZE](https://docs.rs#associatedconstant.DEFAULT_CACHE_SIZE): [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html) = 500

**crate feature **`layout-cache` only.

[Source](https://docs.rs/ratatui-core/0.1.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/ratatui_core/layout/layout.rs.html#218)

#### pub const [DEFAULT_CACHE_SIZE](https://docs.rs#associatedconstant.DEFAULT_CACHE_SIZE): [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html) = 500

**crate feature**only.

`layout-cache`This is a somewhat arbitrary size for the layout cache based on adding the columns and rows
on my laptop’s terminal (171+51 = 222) and doubling it for good measure and then adding a
bit more to make it a round number. This gives enough entries to store a layout for every
row and every column, twice over, which should be enough for most apps. For those that need
more, the cache size can be set with `Layout::init_cache()` (requires the `layout-cache`
feature).

Creates a new layout with default values.

The `constraints` parameter accepts any type that implements `IntoIterator<Item = Into<Constraint>>`. This includes arrays, slices, vectors, iterators. `Into<Constraint>` is
implemented on `u16`, so you can pass an array, `Vec`, etc. of `u16` to this function to
create a layout with fixed size chunks.

Default values for the other fields are:

- `margin`: 0, 0
- `flex`:- `Flex::Start`
- `spacing`: 0

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use ratatui_core::layout::{Constraint, Direction, Layout};
Layout::new(
    Direction::Horizontal,
    [Constraint::Length(5), Constraint::Fill(1)],
);
Layout::new(
    Direction::Vertical,
    [1, 2, 3].iter().map(|&c| Constraint::Length(c)),
);
Layout::new(Direction::Horizontal, vec![1, 2]);
```
Creates a new vertical layout with default values.

The `constraints` parameter accepts any type that implements `IntoIterator<Item = Into<Constraint>>`. This includes arrays, slices, vectors, iterators, etc.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-1)Examples

```
use ratatui_core::layout::{Constraint, Layout};
let layout = Layout::vertical([Constraint::Length(5), Constraint::Fill(1)]);
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/ratatui-core/0.1.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/ratatui_core/layout/layout.rs.html#294-297)#### pub fn [horizontal](https://docs.rs#method.horizontal)<I>(constraints: I) -> [Layout](https://docs.rs/struct.Layout.html)

[Source](https://docs.rs/ratatui-core/0.1.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/ratatui_core/layout/layout.rs.html#294-297)

**crate feature**only.

`layout-cache`Initialize an empty cache with a custom size. The cache is keyed on the layout and area, so
that subsequent calls with the same parameters are faster. The cache is a `LruCache`, and
grows until `cache_size` is reached.

By default, the cache size is [ Self::DEFAULT_CACHE_SIZE](https://docs.rs/struct.Layout.html#associatedconstant.DEFAULT_CACHE_SIZE).

[Source](https://docs.rs/ratatui-core/0.1.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/ratatui_core/layout/layout.rs.html#402-405)#### pub fn [constraints](https://docs.rs#method.constraints)<I>(self, constraints: I) -> [Layout](https://docs.rs/struct.Layout.html)

[Source](https://docs.rs/ratatui-core/0.1.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/ratatui_core/layout/layout.rs.html#402-405)

#### pub fn [constraints](https://docs.rs#method.constraints)<I>(self, constraints: I) -> [Layout](https://docs.rs/struct.Layout.html)

Sets the constraints of the layout.

The `constraints` parameter accepts any type that implements `IntoIterator<Item = Into<Constraint>>`. This includes arrays, slices, vectors, iterators. `Into<Constraint>` is
implemented on u16, so you can pass an array or vec of u16 to this function to create a
layout with fixed size chunks.

Note that the constraints are applied to the whole area that is to be split, so using percentages and ratios with the other constraints may not have the desired effect of splitting the area up. (e.g. splitting 100 into [min 20, 50%, 50%], may not result in [20, 40, 40] but rather an indeterminate result between [20, 50, 30] and [20, 30, 50]).

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-4)Examples

```
use ratatui_core::layout::{Constraint, Layout, Rect};
let layout = Layout::default()
    .constraints([
        Constraint::Percentage(20),
        Constraint::Ratio(1, 5),
        Constraint::Length(2),
        Constraint::Min(2),
        Constraint::Max(2),
    ])
    .split(Rect::new(0, 0, 10, 10));
assert_eq!(
    layout[..],
    [
        Rect::new(0, 0, 10, 2),
        Rect::new(0, 2, 10, 2),
        Rect::new(0, 4, 10, 2),
        Rect::new(0, 6, 10, 2),
        Rect::new(0, 8, 10, 2),
    ]
);
Layout::default().constraints([Constraint::Fill(1)]);
Layout::default().constraints(&[Constraint::Fill(1)]);
Layout::default().constraints(vec![Constraint::Fill(1)]);
Layout::default().constraints([Constraint::Fill(1)].iter().filter(|_| true));
Layout::default().constraints([1, 2, 3].iter().map(|&c| Constraint::Length(c)));
Layout::default().constraints([1, 2, 3]);
Layout::default().constraints(vec![1, 2, 3]);
```

    .margin(2)

assert_eq!(layout[..], [Rect::new(2, 2, 6, 6)]);
```

The `flex` method  allows you to specify the flex behavior of the layout.

- `Flex::Center`
- `Flex::End`
- `Flex::SpaceBetween`
- `Flex::SpaceAround`
- `Flex::SpaceEvenly`

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-8)Examples

In this example, the items in the layout will be aligned to the start.

```
use ratatui_core::layout::Constraint::*;
use ratatui_core::layout::{Flex, Layout};

```
In this example, the items in the layout will be stretched equally to fill the available space.

```
use ratatui_core::layout::Constraint::*;
use ratatui_core::layout::{Flex, Layout};
let layout = Layout::horizontal([Length(20), Length(20), Length(20)]).flex(Flex::Legacy);
```
Sets the spacing between items in the layout.

The `spacing` method sets the spacing between items in the layout. The spacing is applied
evenly between all segments. The spacing value represents the number of cells between each
item.

Spacing can be positive integers, representing gaps between segments; or negative integers
representing overlaps. Additionally, one of the variants of the [ Spacing](https://docs.rs/layout/enum.Spacing.html) enum can be
passed to this function. See the documentation of the

[enum for more information.](https://docs.rs/layout/enum.Spacing.html)

`Spacing`Note that if the layout has only one segment, the spacing will not be applied.
Also, spacing will not be applied for [ Flex::SpaceAround](https://docs.rs/layout/enum.Flex.html#variant.SpaceAround),

[and](https://docs.rs/layout/enum.Flex.html#variant.SpaceEvenly)

`Flex::SpaceEvenly`

`Flex::SpaceBetween`[§](https://docs.rs#examples-9)Examples

In this example, the spacing between each item in the layout is set to 2 cells.

```
use ratatui_core::layout::Constraint::*;
use ratatui_core::layout::Layout;
let layout = Layout::horizontal([Length(20), Length(20), Length(20)]).spacing(2);
```
In this example, the spacing between each item in the layout is set to -1 cells, i.e. the three segments will have an overlapping border.

```
use ratatui_core::layout::Constraint::*;
use ratatui_core::layout::Layout;
let layout = Layout::horizontal([Length(20), Length(20), Length(20)]).spacing(-1);
```
Split the rect into a number of sub-rects according to the given [ Layout](https://docs.rs/struct.Layout.html).

An ergonomic wrapper around [ Layout::split](https://docs.rs/struct.Layout.html#method.split) that returns an array of

`Rect`s instead of
`Rc<[Rect]>`.This method requires the number of constraints to be known at compile time. If you don’t
know the number of constraints at compile time, use [ Layout::split](https://docs.rs/struct.Layout.html#method.split) instead.

Split the rect into a number of sub-rects according to the given [ Layout](https://docs.rs/struct.Layout.html).
